I don't think there's any case of an animal having a biological "wheel" as part of their body.

There are some creatures that "roll" things, however. Dung beetles have figured out how to move their product pretty efficiently in ball-shapes, and pangolins can roll around when they are curled up in their armor. Tumbleweeds act as seed distribution devices, rolling around to deposit them in far-off places. There are also single-celled organisms that look like wheels, but move around using tiny cilia instead of rolling locomotion.

I think the thing that makes the human wheel unique is the axel that it turns around - the wheel & axel is the full mechanism and there aren't any cases of such a thing existing in nature.

Some more info here: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotating_locomotion_in_living_systems
